 Editorial: SNAP fraud hurts recipients and taxpayers, take action now

 Massachusetts continues to battle fraud in the SNAP program. Spencer Platt/Getty Images/TNS 
 By Boston Herald editorial staff PUBLISHED: October 20, 2026 at 3:54 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Gov. Maura Healey has railed against the Trump Administration for cuts to the SNAP program while flagrant fraud in Massachusetts has gone unchecked — until it’s caught by the feds.
 The most high-profile example is that of LaMar Cook , Healey’s former deputy director for Western Massachusetts accused of drug trafficking out of state buildings. He has also been charged with SNAP benefits fraud by federal investigators.
 “It is an unconscionable betrayal of the public trust for a former state official with a pending indictment for drug and gun offenses to then also steal SNAP benefits from the American taxpayer – food assistance benefits intended for low-income Americans,” said U.S. Department of Agriculture Inspector General John Walk.
 Cook is hardly alone.
 In June, the Department of Justice charged 15 suspects for their roles in a more than $1.4 million fraud scheme that included SNAP benefits, MassHealth benefits, and disability and unemployment benefits, among others.
 In July, Antonio Bonheur, owner of a small convenience in Boston, was sentenced in federal court for fraudulently obtaining millions of dollars’ worth of SNAP benefits, while collecting benefits himself.
 Earlier this year, State Auditor Diana DiZoglio released the Bureau of Special Investigations’ Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2025. The bureau’s Fraud Investigations Unit found the largest amount of fraud in the SNAP program, totaling over $4.1 million.
 That’s just the highlight reel. And each fraudulently obtained dollar is one that didn’t go to helping those who actually need it. Imagine if the Mass. bureaucrats charged with overseeing the program were truly focused on ferreting out fraud — think of the millions in taxpayer money that could have purchased food for struggling Bay Staters.
 But the Department of Transitional Assistance is allegedly not “all hands on deck” when it comes to fighting fraud. In February, the Herald reported on claims by a DTA whistleblower detailing several concerns with the DTA’s upper management and leadership, including setting a “tone of normalcy” surrounding drastic increases in SNAP-EBT fraud throughout the state and “in spite of intermittent outcries from staff.”
 There are people apparently seeing fraud long before it hits Leah Foley’s desk, and yet they’re not empowered to take action? This is how you get the U.S. attorney for Massachusetts to create a Benefit & Voter Fraud Team. It shouldn’t need to come to that, but here we are.
 Do you know who doesn’t have to worry about stretching scarce food dollars? The 597 DTA employees taking in annual salaries over $100,000. Who knew helping those in need could be so lucrative?
 The only bright spot in this morass is law enforcement agents like Foley and her team, the DOJ and other agencies on the case. Beneficiaries aren’t the only ones hurt; under new requirements from the Trump administration, any states with SNAP payment error rates over 6% will be required to pay the federal government back for all of the losses. We’re at 12%.
 And who pays back taxpayers for money stolen and fees to cover mishandling of funds? The checks will not be in the mail.
 Gary Varvel. Creators Syndicate
